outcome: TBARS levels in umbilical cord blood
BDNF levels in umbilical cord blood
BDNF levels in maternal peripheral blood
TBARS levels in maternal peripheral blood
cohort: The study included 57 newborns exposed to crack/cocaine in utero and 99 non-exposed newborns, along with their respective mothers.
finding: Newborns exposed to crack/cocaine in utero showed significantly higher umbilical cord blood BDNF levels and significantly lower TBARS levels compared to non-exposed newborns, while crack/cocaine mothers had lower BDNF levels than control mothers.
cross-section timing: At birth, using umbilical cord blood and maternal peripheral blood samples taken at delivery
